## Reasons for the Denial of the Prophets {.passage-heading}

```{=html}
<div class="note-row passage-row" data-p="8"><div class="note-main"><div class="note-head"><a class="note-num" href="../read.html#p8" title="Paragraph 8 in the full text">8</a></div><div class="note-text">And now, consider and reflect a moment upon the waywardness of this people. What could have been the reason for such denial and avoidance on their part? What could have induced them to refuse to put off the garment of denial, and to adorn themselves with the robe of acceptance? Moreover, what could have caused the nonfulfillment of the divine promise which led the seekers to reject that which they had accepted? Meditate profoundly, that the secret of things unseen may be revealed unto you, that you may inhale the sweetness of a spiritual and imperishable fragrance, and that you may acknowledge the truth that from time immemorial even unto eternity the Almighty hath tried, and will continue to try, His servants, so that light may be distinguished from darkness, truth from falsehood, right from wrong, guidance from error, happiness from misery, and roses from thorns. Even as He hath revealed: “Do men think when they say ‘We believe’ they shall be let alone and not be put to proof?”<sup class="fn-ref" data-fn="5" role="button" tabindex="0" aria-label="Footnote 5">5</sup></div></div><aside class="note-side"><textarea class="note-input" rows="2" aria-label="Your note on paragraph 8" placeholder="Your note on paragraph 8…"></textarea><div class="note-bar"><span class="note-saved"></span></div></aside></div>
<div class="note-row passage-row" data-p="13"><div class="note-main"><div class="note-head"><a class="note-num" href="../read.html#p13" title="Paragraph 13 in the full text">13</a></div><div class="note-text">And now, ponder upon these things. What could have caused such contention and conflict? Why is it that the advent of every true <span class="gl-ref" data-gl="manifestation" role="button" tabindex="0" aria-label="Glossary: Manifestation">Manifestation</span> of God hath been accompanied by such strife and tumult, by such tyranny and upheaval? This notwithstanding the fact that all the Prophets of God, whenever made manifest unto the peoples of the world, have invariably foretold the coming of yet another Prophet after them, and have established such signs as would herald the advent of the future Dispensation. To this the records of all sacred books bear witness. Why then is it that despite the expectation of men in their quest of the Manifestations of Holiness, and in spite of the signs recorded in the sacred books, such acts of violence, of oppression and cruelty, should have been perpetrated in every age and cycle against all the Prophets and chosen Ones of God? Even as He hath revealed: “As oft as an Apostle cometh unto you with that which your souls desire not, ye swell with pride, accusing some of being impostors and slaying others.”<sup class="fn-ref" data-fn="11" role="button" tabindex="0" aria-label="Footnote 11">11</sup></div></div><aside class="note-side"><textarea class="note-input" rows="2" aria-label="Your note on paragraph 13" placeholder="Your note on paragraph 13…"></textarea><div class="note-bar"><span class="note-saved"></span></div></aside></div>
```

::: {.passage-body}
1. Nine times in these opening passages Bahá'u'lláh asks the reader to 'consider', to 'ponder', or to 'reflect' on the reason for the denial of the Prophets and become familiar with the cruelties they suffered. The more we observe these denials, He claims, the firmer will become our faith in the Cause of God. Below are some extracts which document various reasons people have given for the denial of particular Prophets. What themes can you identify? 
:::

2. In your discussions you will probably have touched on the imperfections of human character, such as prejudice, self-interest, and closed mindedness that leads to rejection of new ways of thinking and being. Bahá'u'lláh suggests that meditating on the reason for the rejection of the Prophets will lead us to acknowledge the truth that "from time immemorial even unto eternity the Almighty hath tried, and will continue to try, His servants, so that light may be distinguished from darkness, truth from falsehood, right from wrong, guidance from error, happiness from misery, and roses from thorns." What is your current understanding of this truth?
:::

## The Meaning of Symbolic Terms Used by the Prophets {.passage-heading}

::: {.passage-body}
3. In these paragraphs Bahá'u'lláh begins to give explanations of the symbolic terms used in Matthew Chapter 24. He warns us not to cling to our imperfect understanding but instead to 'seek the true meaning of these words' with 'a humble mind from the Manifestation of God'. Below are a list of terms which are mentioned in this week's reading. What was the understanding of these terms among the people? How does Bahá'u'lláh explain the meaning of each term?
    - Oppression
        - Paragraphs [28](../read.qmd#p28), [29](../read.qmd#p29), [30](../read.qmd#p30)
    - Sun, Moon and Stars
        - Paragraphs [31](../read.qmd#p31), [34](../read.qmd#p34), [38](../read.qmd#p38)
        - Paragraphs [40](../read.qmd#p40), [41](../read.qmd#p41), [42](../read.qmd#p42)
    - Cleaving of the Heaven
        - Paragraph [46](../read.qmd#p46)
    - Changing of the Earth
        - Paragraph [48](../read.qmd#p48)
4. While compelling, the idea that such terms have symbolic meanings may not be easily accepted by everyone. For those who cling to the literal interpretation of sacred writings, accepting a symbolic interpretation can seem to diminish the truth of the Word of God. After all, wouldn't it be awesome if the sky literally did open up; wouldn't it be epic if the earth actually was compressed? Bahá'u'lláh challenges this view twice in these passages. About oppression He says:

    > What "oppression" is greater than that which hath been recounted? What "oppression" is more grievous than that a soul seeking the truth, and wishing to attain unto the knowledge of God, should know not where to go for it and from whom to seek it?
    >
    > [Bahá'u'lláh, *Kitáb-i-Íqán* [¶29](../read.qmd#p29)]{.attrib}

    And about the cleaving of the heaven He says:

    > I swear by God! That this heaven being cloven asunder is, to the discerning, an act mightier than the cleaving of the skies! Ponder a while. That a divine Revelation which for years hath been securely established; beneath whose shadow all who have embraced it have been reared and nurtured; by the light of whose law generations of men have been disciplined; the excellency of whose word men have heard recounted by their fathers; in such wise that human eye hath beheld naught but the pervading influence of its grace, and mortal ear hath heard naught but the resounding majesty of its command—what act is mightier than that such a Revelation should, by the power of God, be "cloven asunder" and be abolished at the appearance of one soul? Reflect, is this a mightier act than that which these abject and foolish men have imagined the "cleaving of the heaven" to mean?
    >
    > [Bahá'u'lláh, *Kitáb-i-Íqán* [¶46](../read.qmd#p46)]{.attrib}

    Why do you think Bahá'u'lláh emphasizes the symbolic interpretation so much? In what sense is the symbolic interpretation greater than the literal interpretation?
:::
